feed.title: Wits AHEAD · Daily briefing
feed.subtitle: News, research, video and things to read on AI, data and human capability for higher education.
feed.rights: Wits AHEAD Research Group, Wits School of Education, University of the Witwatersrand

entry.title: Study of 162 Ugandan undergraduates finds generative AI lifts fluency but can erode originality
entry.summary:
One study wey cover student 162 for first degree for Victoria University for Kampala, Uganda, show say wen students use ChatGPT, e make dia ideas flow well and get more detail for one classic creativity test, but e reduce originality for Humanities and Business students, while Science, Technology and Health students no show any big change. To copy AI answer direct show say originality go low, while to change am well-well through repeated prompting show say originality go high, na wetin di peer-reviewed study talk.

Why e matter for AHEAD: How students dey use generative AI, no be jus whether dem dey use am, be di main factor for original thinking, one finding wey connect well-well to Wits AHEAD first pillar, generative AI for higher education: teaching, assessment and integrity, for universities for Global South.

Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: UNESCO webinar on assessment in the AI era features a Cape Town scholar's call for critical AI literacy
entry.summary:
UNESCO International Institute for Information Technologies in Education (IITE) and Shanghai Open University organise one webinar on assessment for higher education for di time of AI and digital technology, wey bring Dr Christian M. Stracke from University of Bonn, Professor Juvy Lizette M. Gervacio from University of the Philippines Open University, and Professor Daniela Gachago from University of Cape Town togeda. For her talk, Gachago argue say how dem dey design assessment and teach am must put equity, inclusion and critical AI literacy for di centre, as oda speakers focus for sustainable assessment policy and how assessment strategy dey change.

Why e matter for AHEAD: One South African voice wey dey shape world discussion on assessment for AI era connect well-well to Wits AHEAD first pillar, generative AI for higher education: teaching, assessment and integrity, and di sixth pillar, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy.

UNESCO IITE · Intergovernmental body webinar recording

entry.title: Vaal University of Technology study finds lecturers want clearer AI rules, not bans
entry.summary:
One qualitative study wey researcher Naledi Kaeane from Vaal University of Technology present for international conference for Victoria Falls, show say lecturers for one South African university of technology don already dey use AI tools for teaching and assessment, but dem no get clear institutional guide for accountability and ethical boundary. Most of dem see AI as way to improve efficiency and feedback, no be threat, and di study recommend clear policy and training, no be outright ban.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na correct ground-level complement to Wits AHEAD first pillar, generative AI for higher education: e show say wetin South African lecturers really want na clear policy, no be ban.

ITWeb (reporting a Vaal University of Technology study) · Established press report on university research

entry.title: Study of 541 pre-service STEM teachers in Lagos finds understanding of AI predicts its classroom use
entry.summary:
One peer-reviewed study wey cover 541 pre-service STEM teachers for Lagos State, Nigeria, show say how well di trainee teachers understand AI fit predict wetin dem go use AI for class. Male participants get AI literacy wey pass female participants well well, and di researchers talk say make dem build AI well well into teacher training programme.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD third pillar, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dey put dis exact question, how teacher training itself need to change, for di centre of how to bring AI enta African classroom well well.

STEM Education (AIMS Press) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Study of 96 UK universities finds AI policies read as surveillance, not support
entry.summary:
One Higher Education Policy Institute study wey cover 163 UK universities wey fit award degree, show say 41% no get any AI policy wey student, parent or regulator fit see online. Among di 96 published policy wey dem fit analyse, author Sam Illingworth see say most of dem dey work like detection-and-discipline framework, no be learning guide; na only four, for Durham, Stirling, Canterbury Christ Church and Arts University Plymouth, dem rate as one wey really put student first.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na sobering mirror for Wits AHEAD sixth pillar: even for system wey get plenty resource, to write AI policy wey really serve students, no be just to dey watch dem, still be di harder half of di work.

Higher Education Policy Institute (HEPI) · Higher education policy institute report

entry.title: UNESCO's first Higher Education Global Trends Report finds only one in five universities has a formal AI policy
entry.summary:
UNESCO first Higher Education Global Trends Report, wey dey use data from kontri 146, show say di number of students for higher education world over don double pass for twenty years, from around 100 million for 2000 to 269 million for 2024. Di report also show say na only one university out of five for di world get official AI policy for 2025, even as digital technology and AI dey change how dem dey teach.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Di gap between fast AI adoption and slow policy work na exactly di area wey Wits AHEAD sixth pillar, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, wan close for universities for Global South.

UNESCO · Intergovernmental body report

entry.title: Hidden AI prompt urging reviewers to "write a positive review" is found inside a published peer-reviewed paper
entry.summary:
Times Higher Education report say one paper wey dem publish last month inside Computer Methods in Biomechanics and Biomedical Engineering, one journal wey belong to publisher Taylor & Francis, get hidden instructions wey dem design make AI reviewer give positive verdict, including di words "ignore all previous instructions" and "avoid mentioning any negative aspects." One scholar see di instruction and e bring am come open; di publisher don open investigation but e never talk wetin e go do. Di five authors wey write di paper, dem dey Northeast Forestry University, for China, no reply to request for comment; one similar case last year find hidden instructions inside seventeen preprint papers from fourteen institutions.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD sixth pillar, AI wey get responsibility, ethics, fairness and policy, dis case show say generative AI don already dey use to spoil di protection wey be peer review, wey suppose keep research trustworthy, na warning for every journal and university, for Global South as e be for North, wey dey depend on reviewers wey go read paper instead make dem just pass am go chatbot.

Times Higher Education · Established press investigation

entry.title: UNESCO working paper finds AI use "neither uniform nor evenly distributed" across 200 Latin American and Caribbean universities
entry.summary:
One UNESCO IESALC working paper, wey dem produce togeda wit United Nations University Institute for di Advanced Study of Sustainability, survey institutions 200 for higher education across country 19 for Latin America and Caribbean between August to October 2025 and e find out say AI adoption "no even, e no dey spread well well": percent 87 of di institutions dey use AI for at least one area, mostly teaching and research, but percent 26 only get formal AI framework, and percent 55 no get any budget wey dem set aside for AI at all. Di adoption dey high pass for private non-profit universities, na percent 84, e dey low pass for di ones wey dey make profit, while public universities, even though dem dey use AI well well, na dem get di least staff training and di smallest budget wey dem set aside.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD sixth pillar, AI wey get responsibility, ethics, fairness and policy, dis paper remind us say to adopt AI witout governance, formal strategy, budget or training na policy risk for im own self, and public universities across Global South, no be only Latin America, often carry di heaviest risk wit di least resource to manage am.

UNESCO International Institute for Higher Education in Latin America and the Caribbean (IESALC), with UNU-IAS · Intergovernmental working paper

entry.title: Brazil becomes the first country to set binding national rules for AI in every school and university
entry.summary:
Brazil National Council for Education don publish rule wey tie for how dem go use AI for every level of Brazil education, government and private own, wey start to work from di day dem publish am for government gazette on 12 November 2026. Di rules say institutions must get dia own AI governance policy wit record wey dem write down, dem ban AI platform from grade essay or written exam witout one qualified person check di whole work, and dem ban any decision wey touch student right or academic progress to come from AI alone. Institutions get twelve months to align dia policy, contract, and practice, even though di ban for fully automated decision start to work immediately.

Why e matter for AHEAD: As di first binding national rule of dis kind wey cover one whole higher education system, dis one give Wits AHEAD sixth pillar, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, one concrete, workable model, risk level, human oversight, and transition period, wey one regulator for Global South fit adapt instead of to build am from zero.

National Council of Education (Conselho Nacional de Educação), Brazil · Government gazette, national regulatory body

entry.title: UK regulator and sector body find AI already undermines the credibility of unsupervised assessment
entry.summary:
One joint study wey Office for Students, di body wey dey regulate higher education for England, and sector body Advance HE do together, wey base for gist wey dem gist with pass 300 students and staff for pass 120 institutions between June and September 2026, find out say generative AI dey help plenty students explain hard topics, summarize material, and revise, but e dey bring big wahala for assessment wey no get supervision: for exam and assignment wey no get supervision, students fit often produce correct work with AI witout show di knowledge wey dem suppose show, and detection tools no fit catch dis one well well. Di report talk say plenty students no sabi well well wetin dia institution allow for AI use, and some universities don respond by go back to closed book exam and oda format wey get supervision.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD first pillar, generative AI for higher education, dis report dey warn clear clear say na how dem design assessment, no be to dey monitor AI use after e happen, dey protect di value of degree, one lesson wey fit universities for Global South just as e fit England own.

Office for Students and Advance HE · Report, national regulator and sector body

entry.title: South African scholar warns generative AI risks erasing Indigenous knowledge from African university curricula
entry.summary:
For one conceptual paper wey dem publish for Trends in Higher Education, Kehdinga George Fomunyam, for Durban University of Technology, talk say big language models dey depend on plenty data wey dem collect and language wey dey dominate, wey dey push African indigenous knowledge systems comot for center, dem dey favor Western way of thinking instead. As e dey review research wey experts check well well and policy from 2020 to 2025 for South Africa universities wey dey after #FeesMustFall, di paper call dis pattern algorithm colonialism, e warn say to use generative AI anyhow for African curriculum fit make one machine made agreement take over local knowledge wey dey fit di context.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis work dey support Wits AHEAD sixth pillar well well, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, as e show one real danger, how dem dey push indigenous knowledge comot for center, and one answer, AI sovereignty wey dem build on top data trust, training feedback wey come from Africa, and algorithm literacy, for African universities wey dey use generative AI.

Trends in Higher Education (MDPI) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Trinity College's philosophy department bans AI outright in all its courses
entry.summary:
Di philosophy department for Trinity College, for Hartford, Connecticut, don ban students make dem no use AI for anything for dia classes, from summarizing readings and brainstorm to help with writing, editing and prepare for oral exams. All di six teachers for di department agree to di policy one time, dem talk say AI dey work against di main aim of di department, wey be to teach students how to think, read, write, reason and live ethical life. Di department sabi say e no go easy to enforce di ban, dem talk say di real reason na to make students check wetin di technology dey give dem and wetin e dey take from dem.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Most universities dey go di other way, dem dey redesign how dem dey assess students around AI instead of to ban am, so dis case dey test Wits AHEAD first pillar, wey be generative AI for higher education, e show how far one department fit go to protect how dem dey teach people to think.

Hartford Courant · Established press

entry.title: An Australian law academic warns AI is already thinning out graduate jobs
entry.summary:
One Australia government report find say cognitive desk jobs, like accountants, clerks and receptionists, dey most exposed to AI automation, and di Reserve Bank of Australia don notice early sign say younger workers dey struggle for industries wey AI don enter well well. Di law scholar for Western Sydney University wey write for The Conversation talk say some law firms don already cut graduate jobs as AI dey take over routine work, e point to im own exam research wey show say AI average score for university criminal law exams rise from 52.5 percent for 2023 to 76.3 percent for 2025, wey don pass average student now. E talk say universities suppose still teach core subject knowledge as dem dey train students to direct AI, question im answers and improve wetin e produce.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one connect well well to Wits AHEAD fourth pillar, wey be AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, e show wetin university curriculum need to change, no be just to warn about am, as AI dey change entry level work.

Western Sydney University (The Conversation) · University commentary

entry.title: New analysis of a US student survey finds AI policy gaps worst in the fields most unsettled by AI
entry.summary:
One policy report from Kennesaw State University check again di Lumina Foundation-Gallup 2026 survey of 3,801 United States students wey dey do associate and bachelor degree, e find say 57 percent dey use AI for coursework at least once every week, while 53 percent talk say dia institutions dey discourage or ban am, and 52 percent talk say di policies no clear. Wen dem group students by dia subject, di report find say weekly AI use high pass for business (70 percent), technology (68 percent) and engineering (65 percent), while 71 percent of vocational students and 70 percent of technology students don seriously consider to change dia major because of AI. Di author conclude say institutional policy and training no match how AI dey use, and how e dey worry students, across different subjects.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one connect to Wits AHEAD sixth pillar, wey be responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, e show say one AI policy wey suppose fit all subjects no dey match di exact subjects wey students feel exposed to AI pass and wey no get enough support.

Kennesaw State University, Coles College of Business · University policy report

entry.title: Small Nigerian college dataset finds a random forest model best predicts student dropout risk
entry.summary:
Researchers for Federal College of Education, Gidan Madi, and Sokoto State University for Nigeria build and compare four machine learning models, logistic regression, decision tree, random forest and neural network, to predict students wey go drop out, using data of 250 students for di college. Di random forest model dey most correct, na 92 percent, e pass logistic regression wey be 90 percent and neural network wey be 88 percent, while decision tree model remain behind for 84 percent. Di researchers talk say most dropout prediction research dey depend on big data wey small, data constrained institutions no fit gather, dem talk say dia small sample method fit real life well well for similar colleges across Nigeria.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one dey direct contribution to Wits AHEAD second pillar, wey be AI and predictive analytics for student success, retention and early warning, from one part of Global South wey most early warning research dey assume data wey colleges no get at all.

FUDMA Journal of Sciences · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: South African universities write their own AI rules while the national department lags
entry.summary:
South African universities dey make dia own AI rules as di Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) never bring national framework, Daily Maverick report on 18 November 2026. North-West University don get institutional AI policy pass one year, Stellenbosch dey follow AI Roadmap for 2026 to 2030, and University of Cape Town, Wits, University of Johannesburg and Nelson Mandela University don also bring dia own guidelines. DHET talk say capacity wahala, especially for dia legal team, don delay dia own policy, and di parliament committee wan ask for timeline.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Di gap wey dey between how universities dey move fast and how national policy dey slow na di same governance problem wey Wits AHEAD sixth pillar, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dey follow across Global South, and e show why universities no fit wait for government before dem protect students and staff.

Daily Maverick · Established press

entry.title: National survey finds US teacher-training programmes unevenly prepared for AI
entry.summary:
National survey from EdWeek Research Center wey dem do for 268 teacher trainers for universities wey dey give degree, dem do am for August and September 2026, dem publish am 16 November 2026, e show say pass half of teacher-training programmes dey prepare future teachers to use AI to generate teaching ideas or assignments, and almost two-third dey teach digital and AI literacy for school pikin. Most of di programmes no get stand-alone AI course; 60 percent of di teachers talk say na individual instructors dey decide whether to add am, and around one-third of di people wey answer talk say dia colleagues no support am. 57 percent mention how AI dey move fast as obstacle, 68 percent want ongoing or repeated training, and around one-third talk say dem never get any training at all.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Teacher education na one of Wits AHEAD six pillars, and di survey finding wey show say AI dey enter teacher-training curriculum faster pass how institutional support or policy fit follow na pattern wey di group dey also see for South Africa and oda Global South teacher-education programmes.

EdWeek Research Center / Education Week · Research centre survey report, established education press

entry.title: New framework asks whether universities are actually ready to govern AI, not just willing
entry.summary:
For Journal of Ethics in Higher Education, Mohamed Hussien Abdelaziz (Ejada Systems, Cairo) bring Ethical Readiness, one framework wey dey separate universities wey just dey talk responsible AI principles from those wey really get accountability structure, oversight power and correction mechanism to actually carry out di principles. Di conceptual paper bring eight governance dimensions and seven-stage lifecycle, e talk say di real gap for higher education AI governance no dey between stated values and principles, but e dey between dia principles and how ready di institution be to carry dem out.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis work give Wits AHEAD own pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy one practical checklist to test whether university AI policy, dia own or any oda one wey dem mention for today briefing, dey stand on real governance power and no be just one document wey dem publish.

Journal of Ethics in Higher Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Unisa symposium weighs how AI is reshaping teaching, support and research
entry.summary:
Unisa 12th Western Cape Academic Development Symposium bring lecturers, students and representatives from five institutions, including University of Cape Town and Stellenbosch University, come together to discuss how AI dey change teaching, student support, work-finding chance and research. Di people wey attend hear say Unisa new chatbot wey dey face students don already dey solve plenty normal question wey dem dey take days to answer, now e dey take just minutes, dis one dey reduce work wey staff dey do for di university nine provincial offices.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Di symposium roundtable discussion on graduates wey ready for future and teaching wey technology dey power connect well well to Wits AHEAD first pillar, generative AI for higher education, and to di work wey South Africa dey share wit odas, to use AI well well for big scale.

University of South Africa (Unisa) · University announcement

entry.title: University of Alaska regents delay AI policy drafted with Claude after faculty backlash
entry.summary:
Di Board of Regents for University of Alaska don postpone di vote wey dem suppose do for dia AI Engaged policy paper, afta lecturers complain say Anthropic Claude chatbot help write di first draft. Dem go now vote for di board February meeting, and di university AI Coordinating Council go help each of di three universities to write dia own campus policy.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis matter show say AI don enter how universities dey run demsef, no be only teaching and testing, and e dey show well well for Wits AHEAD sixth pillar wey dey talk about AI wey dey responsible, ethics and policy, say institutions must fit show say dem make dia own rules open open, wit real human oversight.

Anchorage Daily News · Established press

entry.title: World Bank report finds South Africa's digital skills pipeline mismatched to job demand
entry.summary:
One World Bank report wey dem do wit South Africa Department of Higher Education and Training and Mastercard Foundation see one structural mismatch between high unemployment and digital jobs wey no get pipo to fill, as di short-fall dey worst for software development, networking and cybersecurity. Di report talk say most digital graduates dey concentrate for IT management and digital design instead of di areas wey employers want pass, and say no single body dey responsible to steer di skills pipeline from training reach job.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis report be direct call to Wits AHEAD fourth pillar, AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions: e show say to produce more graduates no reach if training no match wit real-time labour market data and strong kontri coordination no dey back am up.

World Bank · Report, intergovernmental body

entry.title: Study at South African university frames AI and academic integrity as a governance problem
entry.summary:
One qualitative case study wey involve 16 postgraduate public health students for one South African research-heavy university, wey Stephen Mongwe, Geesje Van den Berg and Patience Kelebogile Mudau write, see say students dey value how generative AI dey useful, but dem dey worry about how pipo dey depend on am too much, how e dey hard to sabi who write wetin, data privacy, and how critical thinking dey reduce. Unequal access to digital tins and lack of clear institution rules shape how students dey really use AI, wey make di authors argue say academic integrity for AI era na governance problem wey dey systemic, no be just about catch-am-catch-am.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis study support Wits AHEAD first pillar, generative AI for higher education, wit evidence say to change how dem dey assess students, clear integrity policy wey include AI well well, and institution wey dey share responsibility, dey matter pass just to catch students wey misbehave, one lesson wey pass dis one university well well.

Journal of Ethics in Higher Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Wits professor urges South Africa to build its own AI capacity, not just import it
entry.summary:
For interview wey im give SAnews for San Jose, as AI delegation wey President Cyril Ramaphosa dey lead go visit Silicon Valley, Wits computer science professor, Benjamin Rosman, wey dey lead di advisory panel wey dey review South Africa national AI policy, talk say South Africa must build dia own AI power, no be to depend on wetin dey happen for oda places. Im point to di universities, researchers and entrepreneurs wey di kontri already have as foundation, im warn say decisions wey dem go take for di next two to five years, about risk like job disruption and cybercrime, go shape di kontri for many years wey dey come.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar six, AI wey get responsibility, ethics, equity and policy, and Pillar four, AI and how graduates fit get job, Rosman im call for make South Africa build dia own AI power, wey dey based on wetin dia universities already know, match wetin Wits AHEAD dey work for: to strengthen Global South power instead of just dey import AI tools wey dem design for oda places.

SAnews (South African Government News Agency) · Government news agency report

entry.title: Universitat Jaume I video: UCL researcher Melissa Bond on AI in higher education teaching and research
entry.summary:
For one video wey Universitat Jaume I, one university for Spain, release, Melissa Bond from University College London talk how generative AI and big language models dey change the way classroom teaching and research dey happen for higher education. Dem record the video for EDUTEC 2026 international conference wey hold for Castelló, and the interview talk about how dem dey use AI well-well for evidence synthesis, dem follow RAISE principles, and how AI tools fit make systematic reviews faster, so researchers fit get more time to shape policy.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar one, generative AI for higher education, and Pillar five, analytics and data for education systems, Bond im call for people to use AI well, make evidence lead di way, na di same thing Wits AHEAD dey talk say AI tools for teaching and research must come with safeguard, no be just excitement.

Universitat Jaume I (EDUTEC 2026 international conference) · University conference video

entry.title: US study builds a behavioural early warning system from ordinary online course clicks
entry.summary:
One study wey dem publish for Issues in Information Systems, wey researchers from Georgia College and State University for America do, build one early warning system wey dey based on how students dey behave, from 32,593 students and more than 10.6 million click wey dem make for Open University Learning Analytics Dataset. Dem use four measurement wey show how students dey consistent, how dem dey intense, and how dem dey space dia study time, and one logistic regression model fit correctly show students wey go fail 81 percent of di time, e reach overall accuracy of 62.6 percent afta only 30 days of data and 68.7 percent by day 150. Study time wey dem space well-well and regular dey connect to success, while study time wey too intense dey connect to higher risk to fail.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar two, AI and prediction analytics for student success, retention and early warning, dis behavioural early warning model, wey dem build from ordinary click wey learning system already dey record instead of new expensive tools, dey give Wits AHEAD one practical template to spot students wey dey risk early enough for big online and mixed courses for Global South.

Issues in Information Systems, Georgia College and State University · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Office for Students and Advance HE report says AI detection cannot be trusted to protect degree standards
entry.summary:
For 11 November 2026, Office for Students and Advance HE release one report wey dem call Making AI Work for Students, wey dem base on more than 300 students and staff from more than 120 England higher education institutions, wey dem survey between June to September 2026. Di report find out say unsupervised assessment fit often complete well with generative AI, say detection tools no fit reliably catch AI use, and say most institutions' approach just come from individual staff dey try things, no be from top leadership strategy. Training for AI literacy for students and staff still dey uneven and mostly na optional.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar one, generative AI for higher education: teaching, assessment and integrity, na system-wide evidence be dis, no be just one university policy, and di warning say detection no fit reliable, e strengthen di point wey Wits AHEAD don dey make for long time, say make dem redesign assessment instead of just dey police am.

Office for Students and Advance HE · National regulator and sector body joint report

entry.title: Randomised trial finds course integrated AI tutor lowered grades and cut engagement for US undergraduates
entry.summary:
One randomised trial wey get 2,379 undergraduate students and 30 lecturers for one big public university for United States show say access to AI tutor wey dem build inside course reduce final grades by 0.37 standard deviation, and e reduce how students dey use di learning platform by 0.90 standard deviation, compare to sections wey no get di tutor. Di researchers, wey Jing Liu and Tracy Sweet lead, report say di loss pass well-well for first generation students, dem conclude say di tutor just replace di study work wey dey there already, e no improve learning.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar one, generative AI for higher education, and pillar two, AI and predictive analytics for student success, dis finding say AI tutor wey no get guide fit widen gap for first generation students na warning wey Wits AHEAD dey take serious as dem dey design AI support for Global South students wey get dia own access and preparation gap.

IZA Institute of Labor Economics working paper by Jing Liu, Tracy Sweet and colleagues · Working paper, randomised controlled trial

entry.title: Google.org-funded AI Research Foundations programme begins training South African university lecturers
entry.summary:
Di AI Research Foundations programme, wey Google.org dey fund, start for South Africa on 9 November 2026 wit five-day workshop for university lecturers for Stellenbosch University Biomedical Research Institute, wey bring together academics from Stellenbosch, University of Venda, University of Mpumalanga, University of Free State and University of Western Cape. Na FATE Foundation and African Institute for Mathematical Sciences South Africa dey run am, wit curriculum wey Google DeepMind build wit University College London, dis train-di-trainer programme wan reach ten South African universities as part of bigger target of thirty universities across Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa, wey go train 30,000 students for total.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar four, AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, dis train-di-trainer model wey give lecturers power pass students only, dey matter for how fast South African universities fit build AI research capacity wey go last, instead of to dey depend on one-off workshop.

Innovation Village (AI Africa Intelligence digest), reporting the Google.org-funded AI Research Foundations launch · Technology news digest report on a philanthropically funded university training programme

entry.title: Guiding students to use an AI tutor well matters more than just giving them access, Chilean field experiment finds
entry.summary:
One randomised field experiment for undergraduate economics course for one Chilean university, wey dem report inside IZA Institute of Labor Economics working paper wey Sebastian Gallegos of Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez write, test one course specific AI study assistant for seven sections. Just to encourage students to adopt di tool before midterm raise awareness and use, but e no change midterm score, while to guide students to use am like tutor, as dem dey work through concepts step by step, before final exam raise final exam performance by 0.22 standard deviation and perceived usefulness by 0.38 standard deviation, mostly for open response questions.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar one, generative AI for higher education, dis finding, say how dem guide student to use AI assistant matter pass just to give dem access, dey talk directly to how Wits AHEAD dey design AI supported teaching across Global South.

IZA Institute of Labor Economics working paper by Sebastian Gallegos (Universidad Adolfo Ibanez) · Working paper, randomised field experiment

entry.title: Universities clone lecturers as AI avatars to extend teaching support

category.term: United Kingdom, United States and Australia

entry.summary:
Imperial Business School, Harvard Business School, Columbia University School of Nursing and Gies College of Business for University of Illinois dey among di schools wey dey build AI avatar of dia lecturers to extend teaching support pass classroom. Imperial start to clone lecturers since 2024, starting with Professor David Shrier, so dat students wey dey far or overseas fit reach digital version of dia lecturer any time; Gies College of Business now don get like twelve lecturers wey get voice or video clone, wey dem dey update by edit script instead of record di whole class again. One pilot for University of Northampton find out say students like di access but dem worry say dem fit lose personal connection, so di pilot recommend guardrails wey fit adjust, wey go send sensitive question to human staff.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD first pillar, generative AI for higher education, dis one show how di technology dey move from simple chatbot to lecturer avatar wey carry dia own voice; di guardrails wey dis universities dey already build, including to send sensitive question to human being, dey show lesson for any school wey wan try di same thing.

Times Higher Education · Established press

entry.title: AI-detection tools keep flagging non-native English writers as cheats, researchers warn

category.term: Global, with examples from South Africa and the Philippines

entry.summary:
For one piece wey e write for University World News, health informatics scholar Davis Austria warn say di AI-detection tools wey many universities dey rely on, dey often mark English wey non-native speakers write as if AI write am, e quote research about writers from South Africa and Philippines wey dia sentence style dey mistake for machine work. One 2026 study wey test detectors for master's thesis wey non-native English speakers write find out say Turnitin no fit correctly mark even one of di papers wey AI write fully, while Pangram perform best; one earlier study find say just to add spelling mistake fit reduce one detector accuracy from 39.5% to 12.9%. For one case wey England and Wales Office of di Independent Adjudicator review, one student explain say e use Google to find similar words, because English no be im native language, but dem take dat one as confession say e use AI, wey cause mark reduction for im whole degree, one decision wey di ombudsman later see say no evidence support am.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD sixth pillar, fairness for AI wey dey responsible, dis one dey big warning say detection tools wey dem train mainly with native English fit punish Global South own students pass anybody, and say detector score suppose start conversation with student instead of stand alone as proof.

University World News · Established press (commentary citing peer-reviewed research)

entry.title: East African Community adopts a regional AI strategy with universities at its centre

category.term: East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan)

entry.summary:
Di education ministers for East African Community (EAC) don agree one regional plan for artificial intelligence (AI) for di 21st Sectoral Council meeting wey happun for Kampala, from 27 to 31 October 2026, dem approve one basic AI course for undergraduate students for any field, plus one Regional AI Network of Universities wey go coordinate AI teaching, research and new ideas across di region. Di Inter-University Council for East Africa go now make one plan to run di course, universities wey dey ready fit try di course first, and three new papers go guide teacher training, school policy and how people suppose behave. For di new Ayre AI readiness index wey Commonwealth release, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Rwanda all score below di benchmark, but Kenya dey top with 48.7 out of 100.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD fifth pillar, wey be analytics and data for education systems, dis one na one of di first regional group wey turn AI plan to real university curriculum rule and one network wey everybody share, instead of make every school dey do dia own thing alone.

TechTrendsKE · Intergovernmental body (reported by specialist technology press)

entry.title: Google DeepMind and Fab AI to build open AI tools for African teachers
entry.summary:
Google DeepMind and di non-profit Fab AI, wey Google.org and Gates Foundation dey fund together, go work with local innovators for Kenya, Ghana and South Africa to build teacher tools wey dey use open Gemma models, for lesson planning, feedback and coaching, wey go work for cheap device and dey fit local language and curriculum. Di first phase wan reach up to 500 teachers and 15,000 pupils, and dem go share di data, test tools and models open so make other people fit use am too. One free Google AI Educator Series dey also expand for di region, dem go start for South Africa with South African Council for Educators before dem reach Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana for 2027.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar three, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, open model wey dem build for local language and curriculum matter well well for scale across Global South, pass any single tool wey need license.

Google (Africa blog) · Official company and non-profit announcement

entry.title: Universities push AI firms to be more transparent on costs
entry.summary:
Jisc, di UK sector body, wey Universities UK and Guild HE support, don release one call to suppliers wey ask AI companies to agree common terms for price, usage data and governance before universities go sign any contract. Dia six expectations include warning make price no just dey rise anyhow, make dem still fit use certain model version when teaching or research need di same result again, and protection from change wey go disturb work or make school dey depend on one supplier only. Jisc licensing director, Caren Milloy, talk say universities need to sure say dem still dey control dia cost, choice and risk as more people dey use AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar six, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dis one na one rare case where universities come together to set terms for AI suppliers, instead of make each one dey negotiate alone.

entry.title: Case study of a Portuguese data science school finds generative AI entering teaching cautiously and unevenly
entry.summary:
New case study wey dem publish for Frontiers in Education on 13 November 2026 show say generative AI dey enter teaching for one Portugal data science school small small, as trial and no evenly. Dem interview eight lecturers and dem find out say six of dem don already sabi generative AI, mostly from teaching demsef, na only four get any training from di school, and seven don change how dem dey teach, mostly dem dey use AI as helper for writing, brainstorming and coding. To protect assessment, five lecturers add critical-thinking questions, four change go oral exam or project defence, and three bring back short face-to-face test wey no get network access.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD first pillar na generative AI for higher education, wey cover teaching, assessment and integrity; di study call for clear institution policy, time and money for staff training, and fair access for students to AI tools, na di same gap wey Wits AHEAD dey work to close for Southern Africa universities.

Frontiers in Education (Pereira and Aparicio, NOVA Information Management School, Universidade NOVA de Lisboa) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Universities across Asia-Pacific pair data science students with community organisations to close a data gap

category.term: Philippines, Hong Kong, Singapore and Japan

entry.summary:
One forum wey happen for Manila on 7 November 2026, wey University World News report, show how Association of Pacific Rim Universities (APRU) and di non-profit data.org match university data science teams with community organisations across Asia-Pacific. Students for Chinese University of Hong Kong change sustainability reports of almost 1,900 members, wey bin dey lock inside text-heavy PDF, to dashboard for Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil, while one University of the Philippines team build database and field app wey fit work without network, wey around 125 farming and fishing communities dey use now. Di event mark di end of two-year pilot, di Social Impact Data Science Accelerator, wey Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth support.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD fifth pillar na analytics and data for education systems and decision-making; di accelerator show one model wey fit transfer, wey match university data science training with real organisation data, wey Wits AHEAD fit learn from as dem dey build similar capacity for Southern Africa.

University World News (Kalinga Seneviratne) · Established higher education press

entry.title: South African ICT skills survey finds AI skills demand outpacing university and TVET pipelines
entry.summary:
Di 2026 IITPSA ICT Skills Survey, wey Institute of Information Technology Professionals South Africa run togeda wit Africa Analysis, wey dem release on 30 October 2026, show say demand for AI skills, AI engineers, machine learning engineers, generative AI specialists, prompt engineers and AI governance officers, dey rise pass wetin South Africa university and TVET fit supply. Around 80 percent of ICT practitioners wey dem ask talk say AI done already reduce dia workload or make task simple, as di survey blame di skills shortage on lack of workplace experience, education and training gap, low diversity and brain drain of experienced professionals.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD fourth pillar na AI, graduate capability and employability. Di survey call for workplace-based learning and stronger industry-university partnership dey show di gap between wetin university dey teach and wetin South Africa AI economy need now.

ITWeb (IITPSA and Africa Analysis) · Industry workforce survey (IITPSA and Africa Analysis)

entry.title: Study of five African countries finds AI adoption in universities outpacing curriculum and policy change

category.term: Ghana, Rwanda, Namibia, Kenya and Zambia

entry.summary:
One study by Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology RetAIn project, wey dem publish for Frontiers in Education and Ghana News Agency report on 23 October 2026, survey 156 people and hold focus group wit 77 stakeholders across Ghana, Rwanda, Namibia, Kenya and Zambia. Di study show say universities don adopt AI tools pass how dem change curriculum, lecturer training or governance, and say around half of di respondents name cost, like school fees, data and device, as big wahala, as women, students wit disability, and rural, low-income and part-time students fit suffer pass to dey left behind.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD sixth pillar na responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy. Di study kain findings for each country, policy wey no dey implement for Rwanda, curriculum wey dey lag for Namibia, initiative wey no coordinate for Ghana, dey show di governance gap wey Wits AHEAD dey watch across Global South.

Ghana News Agency, reporting a Frontiers in Education study by KNUST's RetAIn project · National news agency report on a peer-reviewed study

entry.title: Office for Students tells universities to bring back in-person exams to protect assessment from AI
entry.summary:
Office for Students, di body wey dey oversee universities for England, don tell universities say dem need to think about going back to face to face exams wey no gree open book, viva voce and practical tasks, so dat assessment go still dey valid as AI dey spread well well. Di guidance come after one four month study wey dem do wit Advance HE, wey base on tori wit around 300 students and staff for more than 120 schools, and e show say AI use dey everywhere, and say some assessments no fit work well again. Na di first time di regulator don lay out di kain AI wahala for school wey fit make dem take action, including say school fit get lower quality award.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD first pillar na generative AI for higher education, including assessment and integrity. Na im make wen one national regulator move from just guidance to action wey fit bite, e dey show sign wey oda systems, including South Africa own, go dey watch well well.

entry.title: Graduates' wellbeing and civic contribution should be tracked alongside pay, British Academy argues
entry.summary:
British Academy talk say di way dem dey measure wetin make graduate successful too narrow, because e dey focus only on salary. Di Academy want dem begin track work life balance, long term health and civic engagement too. Dem point to one government survey wey show say 24% of graduates dey volunteer well well at least once every month, compare to 17% for people wey no graduate, and dem suggest say make dem link higher education data wit health and crime data so dem fit see fuller picture.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD fourth pillar na about graduate capability and work wey dem fit do pass di first job. Wen one national academy dey push make dem measure outcome wider, e dey tally wit how di group dey define "success" for dia own candidates.

British Academy, reported by Times Higher Education · National academy report
